comments.body:
Thanks for the fix. I reviewed 1347a16 and found one problem that must be fixed before merge: on Linux, upgrading from a pre-fix version can orphan the old daemon. CI is green (14 checks, 0 failing on this head) and there are no conflicts.

On Linux the start time now comes from a `linux:<boot_id>:<ticks>` token instead of `ps lstart` ([host-process.ts#L355](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/1347a16/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L355)), but recorded start times are still compared as opaque strings (28 `startTime ===/!==` sites in `packages/` and `src/`). A record written before the upgrade (`daemon.json` `processStartTime`, the registration lock owner, app-log markers, device claims) now meets a value in a different format. `provesPidReused` (owner-identity.ts:186), `judgeProcessIdentity` (host-process.ts:770) and `waitForDaemonExit` (daemon-process.ts:86) each read that as proof the process changed hands, when it is only a format change. On every Linux upgrade, a new client sends quiesce and `awaitDrainedDaemon` (daemon-client-ensure.ts:154) sees `exited=true` on the first poll while the old daemon is still draining. The client then runs `recoverAbandonedDaemonRegistration` and starts the successor next to the live predecessor. The registration lock also reads `owner-process-reused`, so `isRegistrationAvailable` (daemon-client-startup.ts:455) lets the new daemon take it. If the old daemon hangs, `stopDaemonProcess` returns `exited/already-exited` without a signal (daemon-process.ts:142), and no later client can prove its identity again, so it stays orphaned until someone kills it by hand. Persisted app-log markers become `ownership-lost`, which leaves their log processes running. The PR body's advice to restart the daemon depends on the same comparison.

The rule the code must satisfy: a recorded start time proves a different process only when it was read from the same source as the current observation. A source or format mismatch is unknown evidence, never proof. Could host-kit own one comparison, for example `compareProcessStartTime(recorded, observed)` returning `same | different | unknown`, where a non-`linux:` record against a `linux:` observation (or the reverse) is `unknown`? `provesPidReused`, `judgeProcessIdentity`, `waitForDaemonExit` and `isAgentDeviceDaemonProcess` would route through it. `waitForDaemonExit` then waits for `kill(pid, 0)` to release the pid, which keeps the drain guarantee. Keeping exact legacy matching, for example by carrying both the `lstart` and the token, would be a compatibility path and needs explicit maintainer approval under AGENTS.md.

Could the Linux identity row come from one source instead? In `readHostProcessIdentityRowsSync`, `readHostProcessIdentityRowsAsync` and `readProcessIdentityRows`, read `/proc/<pid>/stat` directly: field 3 for state, field 22 plus a memoized `boot_id` for the start time, and a missing or unreadable file means an unanswered pid. That skips `ps` for identity rows, gives one snapshot, removes the `lstart` fallback and removes `spawnSync` from the sync path. The first decision needed is how to treat legacy records: a format mismatch is unknown (fail-closed, my recommendation, no compatibility path), or a dual-value legacy match (needs approval).

Not blocking, take or leave: when procfs fails, [host-process.ts#L233](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/1347a16/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L233) falls back to `lstart`, so one host can produce two formats and an unreadable value (fail-closed before) becomes proof against a recorded `linux:` token, so Linux should return unknown instead; `parseHostProcessIdentityRows` now does blocking file reads per row, so state comes from the `ps` snapshot and the start time from a later read, which contradicts the one-snapshot comments at host-process.ts:271 and owner-identity.ts:100-103 (move the read into the row readers or use the single-source approach above); `readLinuxProcessStartToken` checks `process.platform` instead of `hostPlatform()` and reads `boot_id` for every pid, so use `hostPlatform()` and memoize `boot_id`; and the tests in [host-process-liveness.test.ts#L271](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/1347a16/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process-liveness.test.ts#L271) only use a hand-written stat line through a mocked `fs.readFileSync`, so one unmocked Linux test would help (`readProcessStartTime(process.pid)` matches `/^linux:[0-9a-f-]+:\d+$/` and equals `readHostProcessIdentityObservations([process.pid]).get(process.pid)?.startTime`).

About the open review thread: the one on two sync procfs reads per pid ([discussion](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4438#discussion_r4539878187)) does not apply, so you can resolve it. Procfs reads are kernel-generated with no disk I/O, and owner and claim batches are a few pids. The only cheap win is reading `boot_id` once per process, which is covered above.

I had no Linux or WSL2 host, so I did not see a real clock step or read a real `/proc/<pid>/stat`, and I did not run the new tests or the upgrade route with an old-version daemon. The upgrade path above is traced from code, and I did not trace all 28 compare sites, only the proof sites. Once a format mismatch reads as unknown evidence, this should be ready to merge.
